plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made up of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. The heads track the sun during early growth and are widely cultivated for seed, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall in the Northern Hemisphere (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated across the United States, Europe, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually a composite of up to 2,000 tiny individual flowers, and the seed pattern follows a Fibonacci spiral.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to late summer, with peak harvest in July and August in cooler regions
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender oil has been used since Roman times, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Hydrangea paniculata
plants.description: A hardy deciduous shrub producing large cone-shaped clusters of flowers that start creamy white and age to pink or burgundy. It tolerates sun and cold better than many other hydrangeas.
plants.location: Native to China, Japan, and Sakhalin; widely grown in temperate gardens in North America and Europe
plants.funFact: The flower color of panicle hydrangeas shifts with age rather than soil chemistry, unlike bigleaf hydrangeas, whose color depends on soil acidity and aluminum availability.

plants.name: Chamaenerion angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower with spires of vivid magenta flowers that bloom from the bottom upward. It is among the first plants to colonize burned or disturbed land.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September)
plants.location: Circumpolar across the Northern Hemisphere, including Alaska, Canada, Scandinavia, Siberia, and the Rocky Mountains
plants.funFact: Locals often say that when the fireweed blooms reach the top of the stalk, summer is nearly over, and the first frost is coming soon.

plants.name: Nymphaea nouchali
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with floating leaves and star-shaped flowers that rise above the water. It thrives in warm, shallow ponds and lakes during the monsoon and summer months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Monsoon and summer months (June to October) in South and Southeast Asia
plants.location: South and Southeast Asia, including India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Thailand, and northern Australia
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (where it is called the 'shapla').
